summary: Yumi Katayama specializes in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. Katayama was attested in 2007 as a PhD student at Hiroshima University and was attested in 2013 studying under supervisor Kenyu Mitomo.

Yumi Nakamoto works in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. Nakamoto held a post as a public researcher at Ryukoku University in 2012 and was attested there as a graduate research student in 2014.
Yumiko Ishihama is a scholar of Tibetology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Ishihama studied at Waseda University from circa 1981 to 1989 and held a post there around 1997.

Yumin Dai works in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. Dai earned a bachelor's at Hebei University (2008–2012), studied at the University of Arizona (2017–2018), completed a PhD at Nanjing University (2015–2018), and became assistant professor there in 2019.

Yumzhana Zhabon specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Zhabon was a researcher at Saint Petersburg State University from 1979 to 1985 and was appointed senior researcher at the Institute of Mongolian, Buddhist and Tibetan Studies in 1985.
Yun Ji specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology, completing a PhD in Chinese literature at Fudan University by 2006. In 2015, Ji was attested as librarian at the Buddhist College of Singapore.

Yung-Jong Shiah specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies, earning a PhD from the University of Edinburgh (2003–2008). In 2025, Shiah served as Chair Professor and Dean of the College of Buddhist Studies at Fo Guang University.
Yungfen Ma is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. Ma was attested in 2011 completing a PhD at Columbia University under the doctoral supervision of Chün-fang Yü.
Yunxi Wang was a Sinologist who studied at Fudan University from circa 1947 to 1952. Wang subsequently held a post at Fudan University from circa 1952 until 2014.
Yunyao Zhai is an Indologist based at Harvard University in South Asian Studies, where Zhai was attested as a PhD candidate in 2026.

Yuri Gankovsky was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at Moscow State University (~1937–1942). He taught at the Military Institute of Foreign Languages (1945–1954) and served as secretary at the University of Chicago (1959–1964).

Yuri Levada studied philosophy at Moscow University (~1947–1952) and taught David Zilberman. He held posts at Moscow State University (~1956–1972), the Institute of Sociology (~1968–1972), VTSIOM (~1988–2003), the Levada Center (~2003–2006), and the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences.

Yuri Parfionovich was a scholar of Tibetology and Sinology who studied at the Moscow Institute of Oriental Studies (~1948–1953), joining as a researcher in 1953. He studied under George de Roerich (~1957–1960) and traditional teacher Bidia Dandaron (~1965–1972).
Yusen Kashiwahara specialized in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He studied at Otani University from circa 1937 to 1940 and later served there as a professor from circa 1965 to 1987.

Yusho Miyasaka was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Chisan College and Tohoku University under Shoko Watanabe. He held posts at Koyasan University, Nagoya University, Chisan Denpōin, and Shuchiin University, and taught Fujio Taniguchi and Shingen Takagi.

Yusho Wakahara specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Ryukoku University (attested 1982) under Esho Mikogami. Wakahara served as lecturer at Hanazono University (attested 1987) and held posts at Ryukoku University as lecturer (attested 1987–1999) and professor (attested 2011–2013).
Yutai Ikeda was a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at Otani University and served as an emeritus professor at Doho University from circa 1980 to 2005.

Yutaka Hirata was a Buddhist studies and art history scholar who received a doctorate from Kyushu University (-1996) and taught Anne Nishimura Morse. Hirata held posts at Nara National Research Institute (~1955–1965), Kyushu University (1971–1995), and Nagasaki Junshin Catholic University (~1995–2002).

Yutaka Iwamoto was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1930–1933) under multiple supervisors and teachers. He held teaching posts at Kyoto, Tokyo University of Science, Tokai, Kyoto Tachibana, and Soka universities.

Yutaka Kanazawa specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology, completing a PhD at Ryukoku University by 2010. Kanazawa studied under Kōgi Kudara, Hōgei Mitsukawa, Isao Shimizu, doctoral supervisor Shoryu Katsura, and co-supervisor Masaaki Noni.
